en.1968_Nixon_Reagan/ending/s0.l73.c13/text:
Order!

Richard M Nixon, how do you plead on 1 count of treason against the United States of America, 1 count of misappropriation of campaign funds, 1 count of obstruction of justice, one count of abuse of power, one count of…

Richard Nixon, as he heard all this droning from the judge, closed his eyes, waiting for the sentence to end. He had been up all night, unable to sleep due to all the stress from the trial. Before he knew it, he’d fallen unconscious. All of a sudden, he jolted awake to the sound of the judge screaming; "NIXON! What do you plead?..."

"Uh, not guilty, your honour… not guilty?"

"On 1 count of sleeping in a court of law?..."

"When did you say tha- actually yes, your honour. The liberal media has been painting an askew picture of me. I was merely resting my eyes."
en.1968_Nixon_Reagan/ending/s0.l77.c14/text:
Hubert Humphrey's inauguration address, January 20th, 1969.

Today I have stood, where once Abraham Lincoln stood and took an oath to my country. It is very appropriate then that from this bastion of America, this very heart of the great men who created the principles of freedom in this country, that today we sound the drum for freedom as have our generations of forebears before us done, time and time again through history. Let us rise to the call of freedom-loving blood that is in us and send our answer to the tyranny that clanks its chains upon the Negro. In the name of the greatest country that has ever trod this earth, I draw the line in the dust and toss the gauntlet before the feet of tyranny . . . and I say . . . desegregation today . . . desegregation tomorrow . . . desegregation forever!
en.1968_Nixon_Reagan/ending/s0.l93.c27/text: The murders and rioting in America will be your first order of business, and more long term, the war on Vietnam. If both of those are dealt with, your silent majority will be pleased. Other than that, inflation must be dealt with, as well as the excess of Great Society. Good luck, and welcome back to the executive branch!
en.1968_Nixon_Reagan/ending/s0.l95.c32/text: Congratulations! Despite the intense battle from Humphrey and Wallace, you have disproven the doubters and redeemed your name. Your performance in debates and campaigning were widely praised compared to 1960, which allowed you to win with a massive landslide. What a turnaround from 1964!
en.1968_Nixon_Reagan/ending/s0.l97.c32/text: Congratulations! Despite the intense battle from Humphrey and Wallace, you have disproven the doubters and redeemed your name. Your lead dwindled a bit as Wallace’s appeal dampened, but your coalition managed to remain intact.
en.1968_Nixon_Reagan/ending/s0.l100.c32/tex: Congratulations! Despite the intense battle from Humphrey and Wallace, you have disproven the doubters and redeemed your name. The bombing halt and Wallace collapsing in the north nearly lost you the election, but you managed to hang on.
en.1968_Nixon_Reagan/ending/s0.l103.c33/tex: For the first time since 1888, the winner of the electoral vote lost the popular vote. It seems many people underestimated how much of an effect Wallace had on your campaign in the south.
en.1968_Nixon_Reagan/ending/s0.l106.c27/tex: After your second loss in a presidential election, your chances of being renominated for the presidency, or ANYTHING for that matter is nearly zero. Retirement and an elder statesman position are all that will await you. It seems Americans will once and for all not have Nixon to kick around…
en.1968_Nixon_Reagan/ending/s0.l108.c32/tex: Despite the environment seemingly being perfect for a Nixon comeback, you had a sudden and shocking reversal of fortunes, and have lost yet another presidential election. Republicans are shocked they have now lost 7 of the last 9 presidential elections. With the margins being as close as 8 years ago, you are already having flashbacks of 1960.
en.1968_Nixon_Reagan/ending/s0.l111.c32/tex: Despite the environment seemingly being perfect for a Nixon comeback, you had a sudden and shocking reversal of fortunes, and have lost yet another presidential election. Republicans are shocked they have now lost 8 of the last 10 presidential elections. Somehow you managed to do worse compared to 1960. Nobody is quite sure how that is even possible, but suffice it to say you will receive much of the blame.
en.1968_Nixon_Reagan/ending/s0.l113.c32/tex: Despite the environment seemingly being perfect for a Nixon comeback, you had a sudden and shocking reversal of fortunes, and have lost yet another presidential election. Republicans are shocked they have now lost 8 of the last 10 presidential elections. Not only did you lose, but you got crushed. Under the weight of two ideologically different candidates, your moderate positions seemed to not appeal. If the skirmish between liberal and conservative republicans wasn’t already bad, it was going to get a lot worse after this.
en.1968_Nixon_Reagan/ending/s0.l117.c33/tex: At the end of the day, in possibly the most shocking turn of events, the popular vote fell in your favour. Nobody is sure what to make of this, but maybe the Democrats can use their house and senate supermajorities, combined with disaffected Republicans, to pass electoral reform?
en.1968_Nixon_Reagan/ending/s0.l122.c27/tex: A return to the Senate might be in order, so you might defend liberalism from demise during Nixon's administration, or gearing up for a run in 1972. perhaps you can do both. In any case, let's hope Nixon can cool tensions in America and bring the troops home.
en.1968_Nixon_Reagan/ending/s0.l124.c32/tex: Despite your best efforts in a tough climate, Richard Nixon will succeed Johnson in the presidency. It was always going to be difficult being so closely associated with an unpopular administration, in a divided party. You still fought hard, and took Nixon to the brink as Kennedy did in 60.
en.1968_Nixon_Reagan/ending/s0.l126.c32/tex: Despite your best efforts in a tough climate, Richard Nixon will succeed Johnson in the presidency. It was always going to be difficult being so closely associated with an unpopular administration, in a divided party. The crime and rioting took a toll on your campaign hard, and Nixon's law and order theme really hit home for many Americans.
en.1968_Nixon_Reagan/ending/s0.l128.c32/tex: Despite your best efforts in a tough climate, Richard Nixon will succeed Johnson in the presidency. It was always going to be difficult being so closely associated with an unpopular administration, in a divided party. It seems liberalism very well might be over with this loss, as you have been crushed. A more moderate candidate in 4 years will likely be chosen.
en.1968_Nixon_Reagan/ending/s0.l131.c27/tex: Your first course of action is to fix what Johnson caused. Vietnam and the riots need to be dealt with. Johnson might not like how you deal with it, but this is your administration, and you'll deal with it the way you do. Act quickly, or you just might become as unpopular as Johnson.
en.1968_Nixon_Reagan/ending/s0.l133.c32/tex: The happy warrior rises! Despite a climate of chaos and a split in the Democratic Party, you've beaten back the opposition and secured a third term for the Democrats. Johnson breathes a sigh of relief after this, and poor Nixon is once again a loser. To the shock of pundits countrywide, you beat Nixon and Wallace handily. The bombing halt and your inspiring words compared to Nixon must have won it for you.
en.1968_Nixon_Reagan/ending/s0.l135.c32/tex: The happy warrior rises! Despite a climate of chaos and a split in the Democratic Party, you've beaten back the opposition and secured a third term for the Democrats. Johnson breathes a sigh of relief after this, and poor Nixon is once again a loser. It seems America is ready to give the New Deal Democrats one last chance. If you succeed, you might be able to rebuild the coalition that's won them so many elections (well, not the Deep South, but you knew that).
en.1968_Nixon_Reagan/ending/s0.l137.c32/tex: The happy warrior rises! Despite a climate of chaos and a split in the Democratic Party, you've beaten back the opposition and secured a third term for the Democrats. Johnson breathes a sigh of relief after this, and poor Nixon is once again a loser. He did quite well, however, so you best work hard, lest the midterms act mercilessly.
en.1968_Nixon_Reagan/ending/s0.l141.c23/tex: As expected, you lost the 1968 election
en.1968_Nixon_Reagan/ending/s0.l142.c23/tex: What happens next is your choice. Another governorship wouldn't hurt, and perhaps you can run again in 4 years if you're up to it. Unfortunately (for you), civil rights will persist.
en.1968_Nixon_Reagan/ending/s0.l148.c32/tex: In a shock to all parties involved, neither Hubert Horatio Humphrey nor Richard Milhous Nixon will be the next president of the United States. Somehow, you managed to come out on top. Southerners are ecstatic, liberals are foaming at the mouth, and the black population has never been more fearful.
en.1968_Nixon_Reagan/ending/s0.l149.c31/tex: Pundits are shocked, trying to figure out how you managed to capture states outside the deep south to win it all. What happens next is entirely unknown. Its likely a crusader against the civil rights bill will happen, as well as the deconstruction of Great Society, and the escalation of Vietnam. Whatever happens, sit back and relax knowing you've done the greatest upset in US political history!
en.1968_Nixon_Reagan/ending/s0.l152.c32/tex: As most expected, you've lost. This isn't a surprise, as you're a third party. even worse, your second goal of deadlocking the electoral college failed. You could run in four years perhaps, and try and win the same coalition, trying to deadlock the election then. You've sent a clear message to the Democrats; the south isn't to be ignored,
en.1968_Nixon_Reagan/ending/s0.l154.c32/tex: As most expected, you've lost. This isn't a surprise, as you're a third party. even worse, your second goal of deadlocking the electoral college failed. You did, however, poll a bit higher above what you were set to win. So good job outdoing your predictions. The south isn't done yet, as you've shown here.
en.1968_Nixon_Reagan/ending/s0.l156.c32/tex: As most expected, you've lost. This isn't a surprise, as you're a third party. even worse, your second goal of deadlocking the electoral college failed. You won just about as much as expected, and yet it wasn't enough. Your supporters are disillusioned that you weren't able to deadlock the college. That's how it is, though...

en.1968_Nixon_Reagan/answers_json/1661@0/de: Medicare is the first step towards socialized medicine in this country. We need to end this program as soon as possible and return health care to the states and to the people.
en.1968_Nixon_Reagan/answers_json/1662@1/de: We need to be very cautious about this program. It's important to ensure that the indigent can receive care, but programs like these always run the risk of adding precipitously to our national deficit.
en.1968_Nixon_Reagan/answers_json/1663@2/de: I commend this piece of legislation. Already we see many Americans receiving health care who would otherwise be stricken with serious and/or fatal conditions.
en.1968_Nixon_Reagan/answers_json/1664@3/de: Medicare is only the beginning of what we need to do in this country. I support a national health care system for all Americans.
en.1968_Nixon_Reagan/answers_json/1665@4/de: How can anyone be satisfied with the course our nation has taken? Inflation is killing the value of the dollar and the gold standard itself is at risk. Unemployment is highest under the Johnson Administration among the very people he claims to care about the most.
en.1968_Nixon_Reagan/answers_json/1666@5/de: Our current economic path is not sustainable. We need to continue the growth we have seen but we cannot allow this inflation we have to continue.
en.1968_Nixon_Reagan/answers_json/1667@6/de: The unemployment rate right now is under four percent. Workers, particularly those in labor unions, enjoy high purchasing power and an ever-expanding lifestyle. Economic growth throughout the 1960s has been outstanding.
en.1968_Nixon_Reagan/answers_json/1668@7/de: The worst thing we can do right now is to sabotage the progress we have seen by continuing to squander our money on a war in Vietnam. I support a full employment economy as well -- meaning we must be vigilant against misguided attempts to raise interest rates.
en.1968_Nixon_Reagan/answers_json/1669@8/de: Whites and Negroes are naturally unsuited to mix together in society. The entire premise of desegregation is a farce, and my campaign is dedicated to ending this misguided policy.
en.1968_Nixon_Reagan/answers_json/1670@9/de: I strongly support what we have done to end the insidious practice of segregation in the South. However I'm also alarmed at some of the ideas I've heard about forced integration of neighborhoods, or the proposed busing of students to distant schools.
en.1968_Nixon_Reagan/answers_json/1671@10/d: We have achieved great strides on this issue in the past twenty years -- and let the record show that Hubert H. Humphrey was at the forefront of this movement as early as 1948. We still have a long way to go, however, before we can truly realize the dream of Martin Luther King.
en.1968_Nixon_Reagan/answers_json/1672@11/d: We need to be very aggressive in fighting racism and its effects where they exist. I support programs such as busing, affirmative action, the new HUD department, and anything else that is necessary to integrate all regions of the United States.
en.1968_Nixon_Reagan/answers_json/1694@12/d: This is one of the most dangerous ideas I can think of. A federal agency to combat pollution will hurt business, increase unemployment, and undermine the wages of our workers.
en.1968_Nixon_Reagan/answers_json/1695@13/d: I believe that existing government agencies can handle the issues we have. It does upset any decent American to see rivers filled with black sludge and industrial waste.
en.1968_Nixon_Reagan/answers_json/1696@14/d: This is something I whole-heartedly support. We have rivers that are unusable to humans, acid rain falling from the skies, and smog so thick in some cities that people can barely see.
en.1968_Nixon_Reagan/answers_json/1704@15/d: Only if they proved themselves capable of repelling Communist aggression. The best thing we can do right now is escalate the war with more American troops.
en.1968_Nixon_Reagan/answers_json/1705@16/d: This should be the primary goal of our policy in Vietnam. It's tragic how many American boys have died to defend a country that is not ready to defend itself.
en.1968_Nixon_Reagan/answers_json/1706@17/d: My goal is President will be to negotiate a comprehensive peace treaty between North and South Vietnam and end this war. That is the only real solution.
en.1968_Nixon_Reagan/answers_json/1707@18/d: I will withdraw American troops from Vietnam as soon as possible. The South Vietnamese should be capable of defending their own borders if they are as afraid of the Communist menace as they say they are.
en.1968_Nixon_Reagan/answers_json/1708@19/d: I will provide as many troops as our generals say they need. One of the reasons we are losing this war right now is because we are not fully committed to it.
en.1968_Nixon_Reagan/answers_json/1709@20/d: I believe that the troop strength we have now is sufficient to hold the lines until we obtain a peace agreement.
en.1968_Nixon_Reagan/answers_json/1710@21/d: We need to reduce our troop strength to the minimum necessary level to prevent the downfall of South Vietnam while we work these issues out at the bargaining table.
en.1968_Nixon_Reagan/answers_json/1711@22/d: Is this question some kind of a joke? We need to withdraw all American troops from Vietnam.
en.1968_Nixon_Reagan/answers_json/1712@23/d: You know, if some miracle occurred and these Communist adversaries were finally ready to explore a new system and allow democracy within their borders, we would be the first to welcome them to the free world.
en.1968_Nixon_Reagan/answers_json/1713@24/d: We should always be looking for areas of agreement, however limited, between ourselves, the Soviet Union, and Red China. At the very least, we can implement arms treaties and avoid the threat of a nuclear war.
en.1968_Nixon_Reagan/answers_json/1714@25/d: The best way to prevent future Communist aggression is not through the death of 25,000 American kids in Vietnam. I support a comprehensive summit aimed at codifying peace in the modern world.
en.1968_Nixon_Reagan/answers_json/1715@26/d: I support a new era in U.S. - Communist relations. We have to be realistic and accept that Communism is here to stay, and work within that framework to find reasonable compromise in foreign affairs.
en.1968_Nixon_Reagan/answers_json/1735@27/d: My God, someone has to step in and protect good order in this society. This is just another instance of federal judges taking control over an issue that's simply none of their business.
en.1968_Nixon_Reagan/answers_json/1736@28/d: I'm not going to comment on a decision like this one. I certainly don't support miscegenation laws by any means, but I also think the Court has to be careful about overstepping the rights of the states.
en.1968_Nixon_Reagan/answers_json/1737@29/d: I fully support the Supreme Court in this decision. I don't know how someone in 1968 can stand up and fight against two peoples' right to marry each other.
en.1968_Nixon_Reagan/answers_json/1738@30/d: Busing is nothing but another conspiracy to mongrelize the races of this country. First it was the Brown decision. Now it's some policy that some academic came up with to send children to school thirty miles from their house as part of some social engineering scheme.
en.1968_Nixon_Reagan/answers_json/1739@31/d: I stand opposed to the legal segregation of our schools. Legal segregation promotes inferior education. I also think that busing promotes inferior education. My goal is to see every child in this country get a good education.
en.1968_Nixon_Reagan/answers_json/1740@32/d: I do agree with the idea that education is a local matter. I'm not especially opposed to busing where local authorities deem it necessary, but I would only use the federal government in extraordinary circumstances.
en.1968_Nixon_Reagan/answers_json/1741@33/d: What good is a Court decision banning segregation if we don't actually do something to integrate our schools? People oppose busing because they oppose school integration, pure and simple.
en.1968_Nixon_Reagan/answers_json/1745@34/d: Can we just clarify my position on all of these fancy programs Johnson created? I oppose all of them. That includes HUD which will infringe on the rights of property owners and increase crime in our working class neighborhoods.
en.1968_Nixon_Reagan/answers_json/1746@35/d: I will do my best to ensure that this program is managed soundly and does not become some kind of welfare program without accountability.
en.1968_Nixon_Reagan/answers_json/1747@36/d: We need to do everything in our power to ensure that our poorest citizens have affordable housing. The HUD department is a centerpiece of this initiative.
en.1968_Nixon_Reagan/answers_json/1748@37/d: Our inflation is being caused by all of this Great Society nonsense that Johnson passed. I will slash these programs, slash our deficits, and end our inflation problem overnight.
en.1968_Nixon_Reagan/answers_json/1749@38/d: The inflation rate we have in this country speaks to the heart of the Democrats' problems in running the economy. They claim to be the party of the working man, but they are fine with debasing wages and property values with their misguided social engineering.
en.1968_Nixon_Reagan/answers_json/1750@39/d: Right now we have the strongest economy almost in the history of the United States. Unemployment is at 3% and our national output is growing at a furious pace. Compared to this, our 4% inflation rate is a pretty minor concern.
en.1968_Nixon_Reagan/answers_json/1751@40/d: The Republicans are grasping at straws with this inflation argument. They know that Kennedy and Johnson have managed the economy far better than Eisenhower, so they are resorting to the only argument they have left.
en.1968_Nixon_Reagan/answers_json/1760@41/d: This increase in crime we see is the natural consequence of integration. I will not allow the black community in this country to get fancified notions of what they can get away with when I'm President.
en.1968_Nixon_Reagan/answers_json/1761@42/d: We have a system in place that gives precedence to the rights of criminals over law-abiding citizens. I will take a firm stand on this issue as President.
en.1968_Nixon_Reagan/answers_json/1762@43/d: We need to improve our policing practices, prevent riots and disorder, and also address the underlying economic causes that spread dissatisfaction with the status quo.
en.1968_Nixon_Reagan/answers_json/1763@44/d: There is a cynicism in our poorest neighborhoods engendered by poverty and by the brutality of the police. I will vigorously address both of these issues when I'm elected.
en.1968_Nixon_Reagan/answers_json/1764@45/d: I wish we would have had the guts to intervene in Cuba the way we did in the Dominican Republic. I will do anything I can as President to prevent a Communist insurgency in Latin America.
en.1968_Nixon_Reagan/answers_json/1765@46/d: With minimal cost and minimal loss of life, President Johnson was able to prevent a Communist uprising in the Dominican Republic. I fully support his actions in that area.
en.1968_Nixon_Reagan/answers_json/1766@47/d: I do support the intervention. We also need to reexamine our policies in general towards Latin America to ensure higher economic growth and more political freedom there.
en.1968_Nixon_Reagan/answers_json/1767@48/d: We have long supported right-wing government in the Dominican Republic, and we've now propped it up against the will of the people. We can't credibly claim to fight for democracy when we do things like this.
en.1968_Nixon_Reagan/answers_json/1768@49/d: Dr. King bamboozled a lot of decent Americans with his rhetoric. I don't condone what happened to him, but most people fail to realize that he was a radical redistributionist and a borderline Communist.
en.1968_Nixon_Reagan/answers_json/1769@50/d: Dr. King is an American hero. I'm proud of his efforts to desegregate the southern schools and businesses, and I was deeply affected by his tragic demise this year.
en.1968_Nixon_Reagan/answers_json/1770@51/d: We need to continue to fight for the legacy of Dr. King. The continuing poverty of the blacks in our cities and in the South is a sobering reminder of how much work is left to be done.
en.1968_Nixon_Reagan/answers_json/1779@52/d: How these students have not been expelled is beyond me. If Administrators want to be complicit in the degradation of a private university, that is their own business. However, I won't spend a dime of federal money on a school that coddles radical agitators.
en.1968_Nixon_Reagan/answers_json/1780@53/d: I will crack down on dope-smoking, homosexuality, LSD binging, illegal protesting, and flag-burning. These practices are the tools of left-wingers and Communists who wish to undermine our society.
en.1968_Nixon_Reagan/answers_json/1781@54/d: There are some legitimate complaints behind these abhorrent actions. I will work for peace in Vietnam and civil rights in the United States. In the meantime, I support the rights of university administrators as they combat this problem.
en.1968_Nixon_Reagan/answers_json/1782@55/d: An arms control agreement with the Soviet Union isn't worth the paper that it's signed on. I won't participate in that kind of a charade.
en.1968_Nixon_Reagan/answers_json/1783@56/d: I would be open-minded about this issue. Without a clear statement of good faith, backed by concrete action, I have a hard time believing that the Soviet Union will come around to arms control.
en.1968_Nixon_Reagan/answers_json/1784@57/d: I will definitely work towards the control of nuclear weapons as President. I sincerely hope that we can work out a reasonable agreement on this issue.
en.1968_Nixon_Reagan/answers_json/1785@58/d: My goal is a world without nuclear weapons. While being mindful of reality, I hope to negotiate an expansive agreement that can put an end to the arms race.
en.1968_Nixon_Reagan/answers_json/1786@59/d: The Pill does not augur well for the social health of this nation. If we could get the support I'd love to see an Amendment that settles this issue once and for all.
en.1968_Nixon_Reagan/answers_json/1787@60/d: We have bigger priorities to deal with right now in America. I don't think that most Americans support or expect this kind of an initiative.
en.1968_Nixon_Reagan/answers_json/1795@61/d: The War on Poverty is a national disgrace. It is a program that steals from the productive to finance the lazy and the shiftless.
en.1968_Nixon_Reagan/answers_json/1796@62/d: We need to focus less on handouts and more on encouraging initiative among our black and ethnic business owners. They will build the prosperity in our inner cities. I will analyze the War on Poverty on a program-by-program basis and cut those which are unnecessary.
en.1968_Nixon_Reagan/answers_json/1797@63/d: I support the War on Poverty as it stands. We have passed a lot of new initiatives and we should wait to see what effect they have. To me, cracking down on the law and order issues is more important.
en.1968_Nixon_Reagan/answers_json/1798@64/d: We are the greatest nation on earth and we cannot rest until every citizen has an opportunity to share in that prosperity.

理查德·M. 尼克松，面对一项叛国罪、一项挪用竞选资金罪、一项妨碍司法罪、一项滥用职权罪，以及一项……你作何答辩？

理查德·尼克松听着法官喋喋不休，闭上眼睛，等着这句话结束。审判的压力让他整夜难以入睡，不知不觉，他就失去了意识。突然，法官的叫喊把他惊醒了：“尼克松！你作何答辩？……”

“呃，无罪，法官大人……无罪？”

“对于在法庭上睡觉这一项罪名呢？……”

“你什么时候说了这——其实，是的，法官大人。自由派媒体一直在歪曲我的形象。我只是在闭目养神。”
zh.1968_Nixon_Reagan/ending/s0.l77.c14/text:
休伯特·汉弗莱的就职演说，1969年1月20日。

今天，我站在亚伯拉罕·林肯曾经站过的地方，向我的国家庄严宣誓。因此，从这座美国的堡垒，从那些为这个国家奠定自由原则的伟人精神所系之地，再次擂响自由的战鼓，正是理所应当——正如我们的先辈一代又一代，在历史上无数次做过的那样。让我们响应血液中热爱自由的召唤，向那把锁链铐在黑人身上的暴政作出回答。以这个世界上最伟大的国家之名，我在尘土中划下界线，把挑战的铁手套掷到暴政脚下……我要说……今天废除种族隔离……明天废除种族隔离……永远废除种族隔离！

zh.1968_Nixon_Reagan/ending/s0.l95.c32/text: 恭喜！尽管汉弗莱和华莱士与你激烈交锋，你仍让怀疑者哑口无言，重新证明了自己。与1960年相比，你在辩论和竞选中的表现广受赞扬，帮助你以压倒性优势获胜。与1964年相比，真是天翻地覆！

zh.1968_Nixon_Reagan/ending/s0.l108.c32/tex: 尽管局势看起来十分适合尼克松卷土重来，你却突然遭遇惊人的逆转，再次输掉总统选举。共和党人震惊地发现，他们已输掉最近九次总统选举中的七次。差距与八年前一样接近，让你眼前又浮现1960年的情景。

zh.1968_Nixon_Reagan/ending/s0.l113.c32/tex: 尽管局势看起来十分适合尼克松卷土重来，你却突然遭遇惊人的逆转，再次输掉总统选举。共和党人震惊地发现，他们已输掉最近十次总统选举中的八次。你不但输了，还输得很惨。在两个意识形态不同的候选人夹击之下，你的温和立场似乎没能吸引选民。共和党自由派和保守派原本的交锋若还不算糟，这次过后，只会变得更加激烈。

zh.1968_Nixon_Reagan/ending/s0.l122.c27/tex: 也许该重返参议院，在尼克松执政期间捍卫自由主义，免其衰亡；也可以为1972年竞选作准备。或许两件事可以同时做。无论如何，希望尼克松能缓和美国的紧张局势，把军队带回家。
